claims: TABLE_INCOMES starts [0, 226, ...] so the worked table shows a $226 row as the free-area boundary
whys: The free-area row is a hard-coded 226, not IT.single.freeArea. After the next indexation the table row will no longer sit on the boundary.
reviewerNotes: The writer's fact question is confirmed. TABLE_INCOMES has 226 typed in by hand instead of IT.single.freeArea.

claims: '... of your 2021-22 cap expires at 30 June 2027 if you do not use it.'
whys: This is correct for 2026-27 (unused amounts carry forward for 5 years). But the year and expiry date are typed in the note, not taken from plan.rows / CARRY_FORWARD, so the note goes stale on 1 July 2027.
reviewerNotes: The writer's fact question is confirmed. The note has '2021-22 cap expires at 30 June 2027' typed in by hand instead of taking it from the carry-forward constants, so it goes stale on 1 July 2027.

claims: Farm Household Allowance advance is {formatAUD(250)} to {formatAUD(500)}
whys: Hard-coded literals. There is no ADVANCE_LIMITS entry for Farm Household Allowance, so this range would not update if the allowance range changes.

claims: Pensions: in any 6 months or 13 fortnights, one advance at the highest amount, up to two smaller advances, or three at the lowest amount.
whys: Counts and periods are typed in a locked list item rather than taken from ADVANCE_RULES, and '6 months or 13 fortnights' should be checked against Services Australia's current wording.

claims: On JobSeeker, Parenting Payment, Youth Allowance or Austudy it is {formatAUD(250)} to {formatAUD(500)}
whys: The range is hard-coded instead of read from the constant. Also, ADVANCE_LIMITS.allowance.label includes ABSTUDY, but this hero sentence leaves ABSTUDY out.

claims: so 13 of them can differ from the advance by a few cents (also centrelink-crisis-payment.tsx line 109: 'It is repaid over 13 fortnights')
whys: '13' is typed in prose, while the calculator uses ADVANCE_RULES.repaymentFortnights. The two would drift apart if the rule changed.
